note: Config home for the cfb CLI (D24). The `weeks` calendar is folded from data/season_calendar_2026.json (D8) — kept in sync by tests/test_cfb_cli.py::test_season_json_weeks_match_corroborated_calendar. cli_defaults are the `cfb` command defaults (config-over-flags, SPEC §9.6). Phase 5 ADDED its §10.6 fields under the `pipeline` key below (kickoff windows, freeze tag, slate filter, data-quality thresholds, Odds budget).

pipeline._note: SPEC §10.6 pipeline config (Phase 5). Every key here has a named consumer — see the key→consumer table in docs/PIPELINE.md. `schedule_et.*.cron_utc` is the one deliberately non-executable key: GitHub Actions cannot read this file, so the crons are duplicated in .github/workflows/ and a test asserts the two agree.
pipeline.dst_note: Crons are single UTC expressions anchored to EDT (UTC-4). After the 2026-11-01 EST flip a fixed UTC time lands one hour EARLIER in ET — always the safe direction for a pre-kickoff capture. No dual crons and no date guards: Actions cron has no date ranges, and a second cron guarded by a string literal is a booby trap. The intended ET time is recorded above and every run logs its actual ET time, so the drift is auditable rather than silent.

data_quality._note: min_snapshot_coverage_pct is 30.0 because the committed preseason manifest reports 39% over 10 slate games — a threshold set from in-season intuition would fail every August build. It is `warn`, not `fail`: an honestly-low-coverage snapshot is still evidence and must still be committed.

odds_budget._note: One get_ncaaf_spreads(regions=us, markets=spreads) call = 1 credit. The D44 cadence (from week 4) spends 16/week — 15 captures plus the Tuesday snapshot, ~70/month, at most 76 (October 2026, five Saturdays) — against 500, so exhaustion is not the risk; a retry storm is, which is what expected_weekly_credits exists to detect. Weeks 1-3 ran the earlier 8/week cadence. min_credits_snapshot is the higher floor because the Tuesday snapshot is the week's foundation.
